title: Ringlet count slopes for first-to-mean flight gaps fell above count ten in two English samples, 1985-2024
abstract: We tested whether the peak-count slope for the gap from first Ringlet detection to mean flight date was smaller above count ten. We used 14,786 records at 891 sites in England and Wales in 1985-2004 and 2005-2024. Continuous two-slope models controlled site and year. English slope differences were -1.73 and -1.70 days per count doubling. Four-test intervals were -3.25 to -0.21 and -2.38 to -1.03. Both Welsh intervals included zero. Knots at five and twenty gave the same English interval signs. This exploratory question was chosen after initial fits and review of prior count-tail studies. It is a direct nonlinear check on overlapping records, not independent confirmation. Sampling of early adults can explain the pattern, but flight shape, activity and visits can also explain it. Missing visits, selected long records, common measurement errors and few Welsh sites limit inference. No causal climate or pollution effect is estimated. Source records remain outside the baseline publication. The package gives code, exact source hashes, aggregate results and independent numerical checks.
